quote.text: Science is built up of facts, as a house is built of stones; but an accumulation of facts is no more a science than a heap of stones is a house.
quote.author: Henri Poincaré, La Science et l’Hypothèse (1902)

stories.kicker: Singapore · the air, at five o’clock this morning
stories.headline: Four of five regions are in the Unhealthy band, the forecast is fair and warm with no rain in any period — and the government’s own guidance says you do not need a mask
stories.dek: The law written for exactly this, twelve years ago, has never been used. In February the minister told Parliament the haze had not reached levels that would warrant investigating under it.

stories.kicker: The Atelier · tripods and tripod heads
stories.headline: The stiffest ball head anyone has measured costs three hundred and thirty-five dollars. The grail costs one thousand seven hundred and fourteen, and is not stiffer — it is geared
stories.dek: A maker told the one man who tests these things that its load ratings are “proprietary”. The layer count printed on a carbon leg is a Chinese retail convention. Almost nothing on the box is a measurement.

stories.headline: Two wide releases opened into near-identical critical indifference — forty-five and forty-six out of a hundred. One took four times the other
stories.dek: The matching scores conceal opposite distributions: critics split hard on one film and were uniformly unmoved by the other. The audience ignored the distinction entirely.

stories.kicker: The World · Hormuz, day two hundred and nineteen
stories.headline: Tehran says the strait is shut. Two cargo trackers, two investment banks and Saudi Arabia’s own November price list say it is open
stories.dek: On the morning its chief executive called the world’s spare supply “scarily thin”, Aramco widened the discount it offers Asian refiners to a six-year low. Both statements came out of the same company, eight hours apart.

stories.headline: Google argued that how much water and power its data centre uses were trade secrets. The state published the report with the figures blacked out, and a reporter dragged a cursor across them
stories.dek: The numbers underneath turn out to be unremarkable. The fight to keep them was not: the same claim was filed over all three of the company’s Nebraska sites.

stories.kicker: The Home Lab · what a merge actually proves
stories.headline: A sparse-attention patch was merged yesterday with a measured fifteen per cent gain on the author’s cards — and the reviewer who approved it had found it two and a half times slower on his
stories.dek: Both numbers are in the thread. Neither is wrong. The threshold heuristic doing the real work was tuned on hardware that is not yours.

stories.headline: The five-hundred-dollar headphone that reads your brain has eight metrics on its box. One of them is a real measurement, and the accuracy figure everyone quotes belongs to a different device from 2021
stories.dek: We carried it at announcement in No. 122 with nothing validated. The first hands-on reviews are in, and so is a named EEG researcher who says electrodes over hair give very poor data.

stories.kicker: The Good Life · one watch, five prices
stories.headline: Omega put the Bond Seamaster on sale yesterday in six countries. Strip the tax out of each and the American list is ten per cent above the German one
stories.dek: The press release carries no prices at all. They live only on regional retail pages, which is exactly how a ten per cent gap goes unremarked.

stories.kicker: The Family Desk · two papers, one day
stories.headline: The two best-designed studies of adolescents and social media published this year came out on the same Wednesday, and both found effects an order of magnitude smaller than the conversation assumes
stories.dek: One followed nine thousand seven hundred children across four years. The other took forty-four thousand daily observations. Neither supports the sentence a worried parent wants.

stories.kicker: The Macro Desk · the regime, in one fact
stories.headline: Payrolls came in at twenty-nine thousand, the market took an October hike off the table, equities rallied — and the long end sold off anyway
stories.dek: Two independent decompositions, the inflation-protected spread and the Federal Reserve’s own term-premium model, say the same thing: this is a real-rate event, not an inflation one.

stories.kicker: The Rabbit Hole · rockhounding and fossil hunting
stories.headline: Two and a half billion Tyrannosaurus rex ever lived. About thirty-two good adult skeletons sit in public museums. That ratio is why this hobby’s hardest constraint is not the rock but the law
stories.dek: The front door is a subreddit called “what’s this rock”, and it is twenty to thirty times the size of any collectors’ forum. The hobby’s own glossary contains three separate words for a rock not worth keeping.

stories.headline: Four weeks of wall squats took nine and a half points off systolic pressure. A new trial asked how little you can then do to keep it, and the answer is: almost all of it
stories.dek: And a second paper, from a different university, put a blood-pressure cuff on people doing the same exercise and had to stop ninety-seven per cent of them inside a minute.

stories.headline: Three of the biggest things on this page cannot be bought. The sumo tournament worth flying for is sold out for all fifteen days — and this year there is no same-day queue either
stories.dek: Each entry here was put back to a promoter, a venue or an official seller this morning. Where the ticketing sites refused us, we say so rather than repeat a listing.

stories.headline: A country has made its daily social institution into its principal export, and discovered that the export market outbids the institution
stories.dek: Kava is 68.5% of what Vanuatu sells abroad. The price of the root has roughly tripled since January 2025, which is excellent news for twenty-seven thousand farming households — and the reason the cheapest shell in Port Vila has disappeared and the lamps are going off in Luganville.
